lines.say: Intelligent people do four strange things.
One. They walk away from fights they could win.
lines.show: %One. They walk away from fights they could ~win.~

lines.say: In one study, replaying an insult like a fly on the wall cut anger and aggression.
lines.show: In one study, replaying an insult like a [fly on the wall] cut anger and aggression.

lines.say: Marcus Aurelius: the best revenge is not to be like them.
lines.show: Marcus Aurelius: "The best revenge is not to be *like them.*"

lines.say: Two. They go looking for discomfort.
In an improv class, students told to seek discomfort kept going longer, and learned more.
lines.show: In an improv class, students told to seek discomfort kept going *longer,* and learned *more.*

lines.say: Discomfort is the signal that you're growing.
Among 15,000 young adults, the smartest were less satisfied the more they saw friends.
lines.show: Among #15,000 young adults, the smartest were *less satisfied* the more they saw friends.

lines.say: Their own mind is good company.
Four. They read people like a book.
Strangers watched 30 silent seconds of a teacher, and predicted the students' end-of-term ratings.
lines.show: Strangers watched #30 silent seconds of a teacher, and predicted the students' *end-of-term ratings.*

lines.say: The signal is always there. Most people just aren't looking.
lines.show: The signal is always there. Most people just aren't *looking.*

lines.say: So what type of fighter are you, in the ring and in life? Take my 2-minute quiz. Link in bio.
lines.show: So what type of *fighter* are you, in the ring and in life? Take my [2-minute quiz.] Link in bio.
